quote: So I was just calling because I got a request here that you were looking into,
stewart_read: Rep introduces self and company but never establishes a credibility anchor beyond referencing a vague 'request' — no form/Tesla-referral framing until later, and even then it's thin.
coaching_implication: Lead with the Tesla referral explicitly and confidently in the first line to pre-empt scam skepticism, per intros.tesla.

quote: I'm assuming you're gonna say that probably doesn't make this a worthwhile venture.
stewart_read: This is a cost/viability objection in disguise — customer is trying to talk himself out of the appointment. Rep agrees with him instead of inverting toward 'let's see what the design team can still do.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have genuinely believed the trees are disqualifying and was being honest rather than reactive.
coaching_implication: Even with real shading concerns, the setter's job is to get the design team/specialist to make that call, not concede it themselves — scope creep into a DQ decision that isn't the setter's to make.

quote: Yeah. That's what I would probably say.
stewart_read: Rep makes a technical viability judgment about solar-under-trees that belongs to the design/closer team, not the setter.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch: 'That's exactly what our design team will map out with satellite imaging — let's get you scheduled and they'll show you the real numbers.'

stewart_read: Rep hedges repeatedly ('I would say', 'probably', 'I think') while improvising an answer about tree removal, signaling both uncertainty and scope creep in the same breath.
coaching_implication: Flag the hedging cluster — redirect technical tree/shading questions to the specialist instead of guessing live on the call.

quote: Let me think about it. How's that?
stewart_read: Customer defers with no timeline and the rep accepts it as sufficient without locking a callback day/time.
coaching_implication: Should have anchored a specific callback day/time before ending the call, e.g., 'How about I call you Thursday to see what you've decided?'

quote: potentially remove that tree, just give me a callback, and then we can build a design as if that tree was gone.
stewart_read: Rep offers a vague path forward contingent on the customer taking action (removing a tree) and calling back, with no owned follow-up from the rep's side.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be trying to leave the door open without pressuring a reluctant customer.
coaching_implication: Rep should have offered to be the one following up on a set date rather than putting the entire next step on the customer's initiative.

quote: I mean, that's I got an email from Tesla asking me if I'd be interested. I hit yes.
stewart_read: Customer reveals this is a passive click-through lead, not an active interest — a low-intent signal the rep never probes to understand real motivation (bill pain, environmental, curiosity).
coaching_implication: Should have asked a genuine interest question here per verify.interest_in_solar instead of skipping it entirely — this is the emotional anchor the whole call is missing.
